text: The Patriots are bidding farewell to one of the greatest cornerbacks in franchise history as Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro, signed a one-day contract on Friday to retire as a member of New England, cementing his legacy among the elite defenders ever to wear the uniform. On the injury front, there's cautiously optimistic news regarding RB TreVeyon Henderson, who declared himself "ready to go" after missing the opener with an ankle injury and is expected to return for Sunday's home matchup against the Steelers, though starting cornerback Carlton Davis III remains officially questionable heading into the Week 2 clash. The Patriots will look to bounce back from their opening week as they face a rolling Steelers team in what figures to be a significant early-season test for QB Drake Maye and company, with kickoff set for 1 PM ET on Sunday. Off the field, the organization made headlines by removing Macklemore as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's performances at Gillette Stadium, with owner Robert Kraft citing concerns over what he described as the artist's "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community."
